slides.title: Decommissioning and Hardening
points: Hardening removes unnecessary exposure and strengthens systems, while decommissioning securely retires systems and data.

slides.title: Decommissioning
slides.teach: Securely removes a system, service, device, or application from operation and handles its data, accounts, and dependencies appropriately.

course.learn: Securely removes a system, service, device, or application from operation and handles its data, accounts, and dependencies appropriately.

breakdown.explanation: Retire it securely rather than simply turning it off.
Retire old server, Wipe storage, Remove DNS records

course.why: Improperly retired systems can leave data or access exposed.
course.example: An old server is wiped and removed from inventory and DNS.
course.check_q: What does Decommissioning mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Securely removes a system, service, device, or application from operation and handles its data, accounts, and dependencies appropriately.

slides.title: Hardening
slides.teach: Reduces attack surface by disabling unnecessary functionality and applying secure configurations.

course.learn: Reduces attack surface by disabling unnecessary functionality and applying secure configurations.

breakdown.explanation: Remove what is unnecessary and strengthen what remains.
Disable unused services, Remove default accounts

course.why: Fewer exposed services mean fewer attack opportunities.
course.example: A new server is configured using a secure baseline.
course.check_q: What does Hardening mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Reduces attack surface by disabling unnecessary functionality and applying secure configurations.

slides.title: Encryption
slides.teach: Protects sensitive data at rest or in transit as part of system hardening.

course.learn: Protects sensitive data at rest or in transit as part of system hardening.

breakdown.explanation: Make sensitive data unreadable without the correct key.

course.why: It protects confidentiality even if storage or traffic is exposed.
course.example: A hardened laptop uses full-disk encryption.
course.check_q: What does Encryption mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Protects sensitive data at rest or in transit as part of system hardening.

slides.title: Installation of Endpoint Protection
slides.teach: Deploys security tools on endpoints to detect, prevent, or respond to malicious activity.

course.learn: Deploys security tools on endpoints to detect, prevent, or respond to malicious activity.

breakdown.explanation: Install defensive software directly on the endpoint.

course.why: Endpoints are common attack targets and need local protection.
course.example: EDR is installed on all corporate laptops.
course.check_q: What does Installation of Endpoint Protection mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Deploys security tools on endpoints to detect, prevent, or respond to malicious activity.

slides.title: Host-based Firewall
slides.teach: Filters inbound and outbound traffic on an individual host.

course.learn: Filters inbound and outbound traffic on an individual host.

breakdown.explanation: A firewall running on the endpoint itself.
Windows Defender Firewall, Linux host firewall

course.why: It reduces unnecessary network exposure at the device level.
course.example: A server only accepts required inbound ports.
course.exam: Traffic filtering on one host → HOST-BASED FIREWALL.
course.check_q: What does Host-based Firewall mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Filters inbound and outbound traffic on an individual host.

slides.title: Host-based Intrusion Prevention System (HIPS)
slides.teach: Monitors host activity and can block suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.

course.learn: Monitors host activity and can block suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.

breakdown.explanation: Prevention logic runs on the endpoint and stops malicious behavior.
Block exploit behavior, Prevent malicious process activity

course.why: It can stop suspicious activity before it completes.
course.example: HIPS blocks exploit-like behavior before execution.
course.check_q: What does Host-based Intrusion Prevention System (HIPS) mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Monitors host activity and can block suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.

slides.title: Disabling Ports / Protocols
slides.teach: Turns off unnecessary services, ports, or protocols to reduce exposure.

course.learn: Turns off unnecessary services, ports, or protocols to reduce exposure.

breakdown.explanation: If you do not need it, turn it off.
Disable Telnet, Close unused TCP port

course.why: Every unnecessary listening service increases attack surface.
course.example: Telnet is disabled because only SSH is required.
course.check_q: What does Disabling Ports / Protocols mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Turns off unnecessary services, ports, or protocols to reduce exposure.

slides.title: Default Password Changes
slides.teach: Replaces vendor or factory default credentials with unique secure credentials.

course.learn: Replaces vendor or factory default credentials with unique secure credentials.

breakdown.explanation: Never leave the factory password in place.

course.why: Default credentials are predictable and often public.
course.example: A router's default administrator password is replaced.
course.check_q: What does Default Password Changes mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Replaces vendor or factory default credentials with unique secure credentials.

slides.title: Removal of Unnecessary Software
slides.teach: Uninstalls software that is not required for business or system function.

course.learn: Uninstalls software that is not required for business or system function.

breakdown.explanation: Less unnecessary software means less attack surface.

course.why: Unused apps still require patching and may contain vulnerabilities.
course.example: Trialware is removed from a production server.
course.check_q: What does Removal of Unnecessary Software mean in this lesson?
course.check_a: Uninstalls software that is not required for business or system function.

blocks.title: Decommissioning and Hardening exam shortcuts
items: Example: Data is wiped and DNS entries removed.
Turn off services with no business value.
Less software means less attack surface.
Need local traffic filtering → HOST FIREWALL
Filter traffic directly on the endpoint.
Example: Only required inbound ports are allowed.
blocks.example: Focus on the risk first, then choose the control that directly reduces it.

questions.q: A retired server is securely wiped and removed from DNS, inventory, and access systems. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: Decommissioning securely removes a system and associated access/data.

questions.q: A new server is configured to disable unnecessary services and remove default accounts before deployment. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: Hardening reduces attack surface and strengthens configuration.

questions.q: Corporate laptops receive EDR and anti-malware before deployment. Which hardening technique is this?
questions.explanation: Endpoint protection installs defensive tools such as EDR and anti-malware.

questions.q: A server permits only required inbound ports through its local operating-system firewall. Which control is this?
questions.explanation: A host-based firewall filters traffic directly on the endpoint.

questions.q: A host control detects exploit-like behavior and blocks the malicious process. Which control best fits?
questions.explanation: HIPS actively prevents suspicious host behavior.

questions.q: Administrators turn off Telnet because SSH is the only required remote-management protocol. Which step is this?
questions.explanation: Unused or insecure protocols should be disabled.

questions.q: A new appliance still uses admin/admin. Which hardening step should be performed?
questions.explanation: Default credentials are predictable and should be replaced.

questions.q: A production server contains unused trialware. Which mitigation best reduces attack surface?
questions.explanation: Removing unnecessary software reduces potential vulnerabilities.
